content:
maria: quick triage — saw structured table columns get swapped in canary after int8/fp8 kernel rollout. only intermittent, seems tied to long-context cache replay mixing types.
sam: can you paste a minimal failing sample?
maria: repro command + a tiny example below. short eval harness used.
```
./run_eval.sh --model rwd-open-6b --quant fp8,int8 --batch 4 --cache chunked --seed 1337
```
FP16 reference output:
{"id":42,"label":"ok","value":0.92}
Quantized canary output:
{"label":"ok","id":42,"value":0.92}
sam: that reorder breaks our CSV extractor which assumes id first for fast ingest.
eden: profiler snapshot shows mixed kernel choices _inside the same request_:
[PROFILE] conv_fp8_fast (55%)
[PROFILE] matmul_int8_vec (30%)
[PROFILE] fp16_fallback (15%)
[TOKEN_TRACE] tok=78 dtype=fp16 kv_hit=true
[TOKEN_TRACE] tok=79 dtype=int8 kv_hit=true
[TOKEN_TRACE] tok=80 dtype=fp16 kv_miss=true
joni: probable root cause: cached KVs stored/returned as int8 are being merged with freshly computed fp16 KVs from the same micro-batch. tiny numeric deltas change softmax order for ambiguous punctuation tokens (comma vs delimiter) and flip field ordering.
maria: also seeing a small uptick in hallucination rate for a subset of structured prompts where the model is sensitive to punctuation placement.
perf-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-12T02:04 — quant-kernel-chooser v3.0 / cache-chunking v1.4
sam: quick mitigation options:
- A: upcast cached KVs to fp16 on read so the merge path is homogeneous (fast to implement)
- B: attach dtype to cached shards and prefer same-dtype execution during replay (more work)
- C: make downstream CSV parser robust to token-level nondeterminism (product-level change)
eden: tradeoffs: A costs ~+7% latency / ~+10% memory on hot paths but fixes correctness quickly. B is preferable long-term to avoid upcasts. C will take product cycles and won't fix current canary.
maria: propose hotfix A for canary and run full eval matrix. if latency impact is acceptable, ship; if not, revert and prioritize B.
joni: additionally, calibration sets were narrow on some shards — regenerate scales with structured prompts included to reduce rare-token scale drift.
sam: action items:
- sam: open PR to upcast cached KVs on read for canary (will link)
- eden: run full eval (1000+ samples), add an assert that key ordering distribution matches fp16 baseline across seeds
- joni: expand calibration corpus and re-run quant-scale generation
- maria: aggregate failing examples and downstream parser errors and attach to ticket
release-bot: PR 4978 opened by sam: runtime: upcast-cached-kv-on-read (int8->fp16) — canary queued
maria: thanks — I'll watch the canary and ping infra if we need rollback.
